headline: South & Southeast Asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel
script:
Good afternoon. Here is your global conflict briefing. The most significant development in the last day comes from the south & southeast asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel, reported by Dawn (Pakistan) 7 hours ago. Full details follow.

Turning to the South & Southeast Asia.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
The United States on Sunday warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthis could “escalate rapidly” after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. “This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly,” the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”. US President Donald Trump also cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Turkiye says it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs.
ANKARA: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia may have military needs due to the ongoing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis and that Turkiye was ready to help under a trilateral defence pact that includes Pakistan. “We see there are very serious attacks on Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity, sovereignty. We have an alliance agreement in our pact. We are in serious solidarity on this point. They may have some military needs, especially on some technical issues. We would have no issues in meeting these,” Fidan told broadcaster NTV.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Two officers among 6 martyred, 8 terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR.
Two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were killed in a fire exchange in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district on Sunday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. During an intense fire exchange between a “security forces convoy and Khwarij”, 23-year-old Captain Abuzar Farooq from Gujranwala and 22-year-old Lieutenant Sheraz Babar of Chakwal, “who were leading their troops from the front, fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom along with their four men”.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Security forces kill 5 terrorists, recover 23 abductees in operation along N-25 highway near Balochistan's Kalat: ISPR.
Security forces have killed five terrorists and recovered 23 kidnapped individuals from their hideout during an operation along the N-25 Karachi-Chaman highway near Balochistan’s Kalat, the military’s media affairs wing said on Sunday. In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan tried to disrupt people’s movement by establishing a checkpost for abduction for ransom, extortion and snatching of vehicles along the N-25 highway, also knows as the Pakistan Expressway, on the night between Sept 18 and Sept 19.

Turning to the Asia-Pacific / East Asia.
From South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Ukraine pummels Moscow with drones on last day of Russian election.
Ukraine launched ⁠what Moscow’s mayor called the biggest ever drone attack on the Russian capital on Sunday, in what he said was an unsuccessful attempt to disrupt the final day of a parliamentary election that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. The drone strikes killed two people in the Moscow region and two more in the Russian-held part of Ukraine’s Kherson region, including an election official, according to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin and...
From South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Russia vows revenge for Ukraine’s election-day attacks as poll shows win for ruling party.
Russia vowed on Sunday to “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv in response to Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow, as an exit poll showed the ruling United Russia party on course to win tightly controlled parliamentary elections. Ukraine fired waves of drones at Moscow and the surrounding region on the final day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze, officials said. Russia’s defence ministry accused Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens”...
From South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: North Korea fires 2 missiles in 3 hours amid tensions over US drills.
North Korea fired two missiles off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second set of tests in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean peninsula through a series of military drills. Nearly three ‌hours after launching a short-range ballistic missile (SRBM) towards the East Sea, or Sea of Japan, on Sunday afternoon, North Korea ‌fired a similar missile, according to South Korea’s defence ministry. If the subsequent launch is confirmed to be a ballistic...
From Taipei Times, just now: US warns of escalation after attack on Riyadh.

Turning to the Russia's Conflicts.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russia threatens to further intensify attacks on Kyiv following hits in Moscow.
Russia’s Defence Ministry threatened to increase strikes on military targets in Kyiv following reported Ukrainian drone and missile attacks on Moscow and Moscow Oblast.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russians attack Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast: five injured.
Russian forces attacked Dnipropetrovsk Oblast over 50 times with drones and artillery on 20 September, injuring five people and damaging homes in Nikopol.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russian UAVs cause fire in warehouses and damage businesses in Kyiv Oblast – video.
Russian UAVs attack three districts in Kyiv Oblast, damaging company buildings and vehicles and causing warehouse fires in Boryspil district.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps deploys air-dropped kamikaze UGV for the first time during offensive in Donetsk Oblast.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps air-dropped kamikaze UGVs over 10 km behind Russian lines using bomber drones to liberate two villages in Donetsk Oblast.

Turning to the Middle East.
From Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: Iran claims US preparing to resume attacks, threatens bases, supporting regional countries.
The military said that any US attack would trigger sustained strikes on US bases and interests in the region, the report added.
From Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: 'No terrorist is immune,' Netanyahu says as IDF chief orders reinforcements to join manhunt.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir affirmed that should the terrorist who carried out the shooting attack is not killed during the manhunt, "he belongs on the gallows."
From Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: How will Saudi Arabia deal with the Houthis?.
Yemeni group warns of further attacks on the kingdom.
From Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Man Utd salvage Fulham draw as pressure mounts on Carrick.
Matheus Cunha strikes late as Manchester United seal a 1-1 draw at Fulham, but pressure mounts on Michael Carrick.

Turning to the Korean Peninsula.

From NK News, 14 hours ago: North Korea launches suspected ballistic missiles toward East Sea: JCS.
North Korea launched suspected ballistic missiles toward the East Sea (Sea of Japan) twice on Sunday, according to South Korean and Japanese authorities. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) reported that it detected a ballistic missile launched from Wonsan on North Korea’s east coast around 3 p.m. KST. The missile flew approximately 280 miles […]

Turning to the Europe (non-Russia).
From Politico Europe, 11 hours ago: Massive Ukrainian drone attack hits Moscow on last day of Russian elections.
"This unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the ⁠elections," said Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin.

Turning to the Africa.
From Africanews, 8 hours ago: Gaza children return to school after years of war and displacement.
Children in Gaza are heading back to school as a new academic year begins, returning to classrooms that remain heavily damaged and lacking basic equipment after years of war.
From Africanews, 10 hours ago: Uganda suspends military cooperation with Turkey amid political tensions.
Uganda's army said Saturday it had suspended military cooperation with Turkey, after demands for Ankara to hand over a prominent political blogger and fierce critic of President Yoweri Museveni.
From Africanews, 11 hours ago: Congo launches Ebola vaccination campaign for frontline workers.
Congo began vaccinating health care workers against Ebola on Saturday in Bunia, the epicenter of the fastest-growing outbreak of the disease in the country’s history.
From Africanews, 14 hours ago: Nigeria appoints panel to probe deaths of 37 miners in holding cell.
Nigeria's government has appointed a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 people in a paramilitary civil defence force holding cell, the interior minister said Saturday.

Turning to the The Americas.
From Buenos Aires Herald, 7 hours ago: Twenty years without Jorge Julio López, the man who disappeared twice.
López was kidnapped by the military dictatorship in 1976. In 2006, he disappeared again after testifying against his captor La entrada Twenty years without Jorge Julio López, the man who disappeared twice se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

United States: no notable new developments in the last 48 hours.
